messages:
liam: quick note  postdeploy smoke for v0.24.3 canary (3%) shows sporadic kvprobe p95 spikes correlated with large GC pauses on canary-usw1-02. attaching short trace.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: v0.24.3 -> canary=3% (hosts: canary-usw1-01..03)
nina: observed three distinct 400-600ms spikes between 14:10-14:15UTC, all from canary-usw1-02. no increase in 5xx.
infra-oncall: digging into node logs: JVM GC pause events at 14:10:05 and 14:12:22 on canary-usw1-02, pause durations ~300-420ms. heap pressure low otherwise.
sam: synth log snippet:
```
[2026-03-21T14:10:06Z] kvprobe id=xy12 latency=412ms status=200
[2026-03-21T14:12:23Z] kvprobe id=xy13 latency=395ms status=200
```
qa-bot: pre-deploy baseline p95=85ms, postdeploy p95=220ms on canary ring (driven by the one host).
liam: proposal: pause ramp and remove canary-usw1-02 from rotation (drain) while infra investigates GC collector settings. keep canary at 2% using remaining hosts.
infra-oncall: will cordon+drain canary-usw1-02 now and redeploy with adjusted JVM flags if needed. ETA 8m.
sam: agree with drain. no customer-facing rollback yet; spikes are single-host and not impacting errors.
deploy-bot: Canary ramp paused per request by liam. Adjusting canary target to 2%.
infra-oncall: cordoned canary-usw1-02, draining connections. monitoring.
qa-bot: quick probe after drain: canary p95=90ms, spikes gone in sample window.
liam: consensus: hold rollout, keep change-window open but pin production to v0.24.2. create follow-up ticket INF-1309 to capture GC tuning and add a synthetic test that stresses heap to catch similar regressions earlier.
infra-oncall: creating INF-1309 and will attach GC dumps from canary-usw1-02 if pauses recur.
liam: thanks. we'll reattempt rollout once INF-1309 has recommended JVM flags and we run a targeted canary with verbose GC and extended synthetic coverage.
